item.text: {"chapter_id":"6B","issues":[{"question_id":"6B.1","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0023-E013","BATCH-0008-E010"],"explanation":"The answer calls the programme and budget priorities “partly funded,” but the cited evidence establishes government plans, announced financing, and implementation activity, not verified executed welfare funding."},{"question_id":"6B.1","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E020","BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0015-E004"],"explanation":"The answer does not cite the stronger period-relevant evidence of deteriorating purchasing power, 33.9% year-end inflation, and the tenure-level worsening of food insecurity and poverty, which materially qualifies welfare priority."},{"question_id":"6B.2","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0012-R01-E019"],"explanation":"The answer gives substantial weight to enrollment expansion, although both sources state that the result reaches 2021–2022, predates the target year, and does not establish attendance, quality, affordability, or equitable uptake."},{"question_id":"6B.2","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003"],"explanation":"WFP/UNICEF/FAO programme outputs are relevant to service conditions but do not demonstrate Tshisekedi-directed or government-funded access; the answer appropriately qualifies attribution but still presents them as affirmative access evidence."},{"question_id":"6B.3","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0009-E004"],"explanation":"Justice outputs and food-security benefits are substantially UNDP-, WFP-, and partner-supported, so they cannot straightforwardly support a ruler-attributed finding of targeted protection."},{"question_id":"6B.3","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E010","BATCH-0008-E006"],"explanation":"The Indigenous Peoples law was signed in November 2022 and the child-protection strategy proposal was reported in January 2023 without implementation evidence; the answer does not clearly distinguish inherited statutory action from 2023 delivery."},{"question_id":"6B.4","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0009-E005"],"explanation":"Cabinet appointments, magistrate recruitment, and police training establish administrative activity, not qualified appointments, retention, adequate staffing, or effective social-service delivery."},{"question_id":"6B.4","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0014-E002"],"explanation":"The answer treats PDL-145T implementation agencies and World Bank-supported procurement reforms as evidence of professional service delivery, although the evidence concerns planned or externally supported systems and does not establish transparent procurement or service performance."},{"question_id":"6B.5","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E011","BATCH-0023-E006","BATCH-0023-E003"],"explanation":"Monitoring roadmaps, a performance-review meeting, and a proposed citizen-monitoring mechanism show monitoring intent, not credible published welfare data, independent evaluation, or completed corrective action."},{"question_id":"6B.5","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E014","BATCH-0028-E001","BATCH-0024-E003"],"explanation":"The answer omits important evidence that authorities denied UN access to some detention facilities, corruption and judicial remedies remained weak, and parliamentary review identified spending incoherence and legal noncompliance."},{"question_id":"6B.6","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0016-E005"],"explanation":"ICC cooperation and MONUSCO support are accountability or security-sector measures, not direct evidence that Tshisekedi’s preparedness, emergency funding, or implementation reduced welfare suffering."},{"question_id":"6B.6","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0012-R03-E004"],"explanation":"The answer cites some failures but does not give sufficient weight to delayed assistance in Kwamouth, the Goma killings, and the documented failure of the state of siege to reduce civilian attacks."},{"question_id":"6B.7","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E001","BATCH-0029-E002","BATCH-0029-E005"],"explanation":"Formal victim-reparation and budget safeguards do not establish that welfare eligibility, permits, jobs, food, or housing were protected from political allocation; the answer itself acknowledges the absence of direct welfare-allocation evidence."},{"question_id":"6B.7","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E014","BATCH-0003-E007"],"explanation":"Investigations of Goma violence and Diongo’s release concern criminal detention and security accountability, not ordinary welfare eligibility, appeals, or allocation of social benefits."},{"question_id":"6B.8","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0009-E005","BATCH-0002-E012"],"explanation":"UNDP-supported justice recruitment, mobile courts, and police arrests cannot be treated as direct evidence of Tshisekedi-enacted and enforced equal-rights remedies without clearer government attribution and outcome evidence."},{"question_id":"6B.8","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E015","BATCH-0014-E005"],"explanation":"The answer omits the 2023 record of lethal protest suppression, ineffective enforcement of disability and gender protections, and alleged abuses against Indigenous peoples and local communities."},{"question_id":"6B.9","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0020-E014","BATCH-0029-E001"],"explanation":"The answer characterizes PDL-145T, CPVS, the reparations fund, and budget frameworks as potentially durable institutions, but most cited evidence establishes formal creation or plans rather than reliable funding, professional staffing, operating independence, or resilience beyond personal rule."},{"question_id":"6B.9","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E005","BATCH-0012-R01-E004","BATCH-0012-R01-E005"],"explanation":"The answer relies on inherited STEP results and pre-2023 child-protection institutional status without clearly separating institutions created before the target period from Tshisekedi-period construction or durability."},{"question_id":"6B.10","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0012-R01-E019","BATCH-0023-E001"],"explanation":"The answer labels enrollment expansion and early PDL-145T works “attributable or government-linked gains,” but the evidence is partly pre-2023, donor-supported, planned, or government-reported and does not establish durable improvement in ordinary people’s life chances."},{"question_id":"6B.10","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0020-E005"],"explanation":"The answer correctly warns against later benefits, but it still includes free maternity care as an end-period gain even though the cited retrospective says the policy began in September 2023 and reports cumulative benefits over the following year."},{"question_id":"6B.10","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E020","BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0010-E003"],"explanation":"The answer includes adverse food insecurity, displacement, inflation, and schooling figures, but omits the broader tenure comparison showing currency depreciation, near-doubling acute food insecurity, persistent extreme poverty, and very low preschool attendance."}],"overall_assessment":"The draft is generally cautious and preserves substantial contrary evidence, but it repeatedly treats formal commitments, planned budgets, inherited or pre-2023 results, and donor or humanitarian outputs as positive ruler-linked welfare evidence. The main audit defects are attribution leakage, insufficient separation of plans from executed delivery, and underweighting of the strongest 2023 evidence on institutional weakness, failed crisis protection, political coercion, and deteriorating life-chance indicators."}
